definition: The 18 states that were never on the pre-14th-FC special-category list. Defined by exclusion: every `kind: state` in states.json minus the `special_category` legacy 11 (less J&K which became a UT in 2019, leaving 10 of the 11 still as states; 28 − 10 = 18). The 14th Finance Commission (2015) folded the 30%-special-plan-assistance regime into the 42% horizontal devolution pool; 'general' here is therefore a fiscal residual, not a constitutional category. Used as the default peer set for fiscal indicators where comparing across the asymmetric centre-transfer regime would be misleading (e.g. outstanding-debt-pct-GSDP).
notes: Andhra Pradesh (S01) is included here. The 2014 Reorganisation Act promised special-category status; the Centre never notified it. We follow notification, not promise.

definition: States and UTs whose territory is dominated by the Himalayan range, used as a peer set for topographical / agro-climatic comparisons (forest cover, hydropower potential, climate vulnerability). Includes the eastern Himalayan stretch (Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura), the western Himalayan stretch (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand), and the trans-Himalayan UTs (Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh). Excludes Assam (Brahmaputra plain, not Himalayan). Distinct from `neh` (which is a statutory FC funding window with different membership and different policy citations) per panel decision — set near-equality is not grounds for merging when the two tiers are cited by different authorities.

Sui generis singleton tier for the National Capital Territory of Delhi under Article 239AA. Delhi has an elected Legislative Assembly with circumscribed powers — police, public order and land are reserved to the Centre via the Lieutenant Governor (per the 2021 GNCTD Amendment Act). Singleton because comparing Delhi against either Puducherry (`ut_legislature`) or full states is a category error: Delhi has VAT/GST on a metropolitan consumption base that Puducherry lacks, but lacks land-use authority that any state has.
authority: Article 239AA; Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act 1991; GNCTD (Amendment) Act 2021

definition: The 11 states historically conferred Special-Category Status (SCS) by successive Finance Commissions and the National Development Council from 1969 onwards: Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, Jammu & Kashmir (now a UT, retained here for fiscal-history continuity), Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand. The 14th Finance Commission (2015) discontinued SCS as a fiscal devolution category, but the Centre still applies the 90:10 Centrally-Sponsored Scheme funding ratio to these 11 (vs 60:40 for general-category states). The category is dead in FC arithmetic, alive in CSS arithmetic; ignoring it would misread MGNREGA / PMAY / JJM transfer comparisons.
authority: Pre-14th-FC NDC resolutions (1969 onwards); 14th Finance Commission Report (2015) for discontinuation; current operative use: Ministry of Finance Rationalisation of CSS OM (2021)
notes: U08 (Jammu & Kashmir) appears here AND in `ut_legislature` — this dual membership is intentional. The fiscal history the indicator is comparing predates the 2019 reorganisation.
